PullRequest.Title: Preserve cached token usage in Agent Host BYOK responses
PullRequest.Body:
The Copilot harness reports zero cached tokens for BYOK responses even when the provider supplies a cache-hit count. This affects usage display, telemetry, and cost estimation.

- **Bridge:** Carry `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` from provider usage to the Agent Host.
- **Responses:** Emit the count in streamed and non-streamed responses, defaulting to zero when unavailable.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #348390

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host BYOK chat with streamed Responses output, including provider cache hits and missing usage details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing loopback HTTP request invokes one renderer bridge chat call, which invokes the selected LM provider. Text/reasoning/tool deltas can reach the client before completion. Usage is decoded from existing provider usage parts and serialized into the final response.completed frame only after response.result and stream consumption finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive the SDK's loopback Responses HTTP request and write SSE frames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTTP request per model invocation, existing incremental SSE frames, and one final completed frame.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical HTTP and frame counts; final input_tokens_details.cached_tokens was always zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing streaming response path; the changed numeric value appears only in final usage metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward chat to the renderer and return the accumulated result; forward existing stream deltas separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bridge chat RPC per invocation plus existing deltas. One optional number is added to the existing result, not to each delta.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same chat result traversed the bridge without cachedTokens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bridge completion already gates final usage emission; no new hop or await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the extension-provided language model through $startChatRequest and consume its existing progress stream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider-start RPC per chat request and the provider's existing response parts; no added provider invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same messages and options were sent to the same provider; prompt_tokens_details was already present in its usage payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider output already gates chat progress. Any provider-owned network work remains unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse an existing usage payload and serialize the final usage envelope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same JSON parse per provider usage part and same final frame serialization. Added extraction is bounded property access and one numeric DTO field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Usage JSON was already fully parsed, and the same cached_tokens output field already existed with value zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant additional work within existing parsing and completion; no additional full-response copy or serialization pass.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Concurrent model requests, provider stream parts, and response size. Added work is constant per usage part and one numeric lookup per completed response; it does not scale with the cached-token count or conversation history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parts are folded sequentially within each request; provider completion and stream consumption are awaited together. Independent requests retain existing concurrency. No extra tasks, requests, subscriptions, or limiter changes are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: cachedTokens is accounting metadata, not a cache lookup or cache-control input. Cold provider requests, cache-hit requests, absent details, and explicit zero all use the same existing request path. Provider prompt cache keys and continuation maps are unchanged; no cache, negative-cache entry, or coalescing behavior is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced handler stream consumption, reverse IPC adapter, provider dispatch, proxy completion, and SSE usage-envelope call site.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency, chunk count, and request concurrency vary, but the diff introduces only bounded scalar handling and does not change boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression. This preserves existing metadata without changing expensive work, scheduling, cache behavior, or retained lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host BYOK chat with a buffered, non-streamed Responses body
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The proxy awaits the same bridge/provider request and completed stream, then prepares and JSON-stringifies one final Responses body. The added cached-token lookup executes during existing usage-envelope construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return a JSON Responses body over the existing loopback HTTP connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One HTTP response body per successful invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same response body was emitted, with cached_tokens fixed to zero.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Body still waits for provider completion; no new prerequisite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing renderer chat RPC and extension-provider start RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bridge call and one provider-start call per model request, with existing provider progress; only the final bridge result gains one optional numeric property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same RPC count, messages, provider options, and completion wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both were already on the critical path and remain in the same order.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and stringify the existing completed Responses envelope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing body serialization per successful request; no new pass over output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical envelope shape and serialization operation; only the cached_tokens value differed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing final-response serialization with one scalar lookup changed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One usage envelope per completed request. Existing response conversion and serialization scale with output size; the changed work and extra bridge payload remain constant-sized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited bridge call per HTTP request; no renderer delta emitter for requests without requestId. Existing independent-request concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cache-hit counts are passed through as numbers; missing details default to zero in the existing output shape. No response cache or invalidation policy changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both buffered and streamed production call sites share the changed usageEnvelope, and all diff pages were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Output size and provider duration vary; neither multiplies the added scalar processing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The response already allocated input_tokens_details and serialized cached_tokens before this change.

Scenarios.Scenario: BYOK utility-model completion using the shared renderer handler
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentHostUtilityModelService._byokChatCompletion awaits one bridge chat result and extracts its text. The shared handler now includes cachedTokens in usage, but utility text processing and its existing telemetry projection do not consume the new field.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing utility request to renderer and subsequent provider dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bridge chat RPC and one existing provider invocation per utility completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same request and result path, with no cachedTokens property in decoded usage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already awaited before text can be returned. No additional call or wait.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing restricted-telemetry context resolution and telemetry reporting, where applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing context-resolution call and report scheduling per utility invocation; any service-level caching remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical telemetry scheduling and projected fields; cachedTokens is not read by this utility report.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution starts before chat and reporting chains off its promise without gating the returned text.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-sized usage addition per utility invocation, independent of utility message or response length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing raceAbort wait around a single bridge request; telemetry account resolution and reporting remain asynchronous and are not awaited before returning text.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new count does not affect provider selection, request options, telemetry account resolution, or caching. No new retained cache entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected utility bridge invocation, usage projection, text extraction, and asynchronous telemetry scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider and telemetry implementations vary; their work and scheduling are untouched by this scalar DTO addition.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable regression on this additional caller of the changed handler.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all five changed files and every diff page. Traced usage decoding, bridge transport, provider dispatch, streamed and buffered response serialization, and the shared utility caller. The diff only preserves a numeric usage field; no high-confidence introduced performance issue or concrete performance-regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
